point: The language we use to define disability directly shapes how we value and perceive people.
quote: our language affects our thinking and how we view the world and how we view other people

point: Supportive adults can fundamentally transform how children perceive their own strength and identity.
quote: this is an example of how adults in positions of power can ignite the power of a child

point: Humanity's greatest strength lies in our innate ability to adapt to changes and challenges.
quote: everyone has something rare and powerful to offer our society and that the human ability to adapt is our greatest asset

point: Adversity is an intrinsic part of life that shapes us rather than an obstacle we must avoid.
quote: adversity isn't an obstacle that we need to get around in order to resume living our life it's part of our life

point: Focusing exclusively on fixing what is perceived as broken can be more harmful than the underlying condition.
quote: perhaps the existing model of only looking at what is broken in you and how do we fix it serves to be more disabling

point: Human growth and resilience are sparked when people struggle through conflict and transform.
quote: the human ability to survive and flourish is driven by the the struggle of the human spirit through conflict into transformation

point: Shifting away from the illusion of normalcy toward potential allows people to fully share their unique abilities.
quote: if we can change this paradigm from one of achieving normalcy to one of possibility or potency

point: Medical prognoses fail to account for the immense, unquantifiable power of the human will.
quote: no prognosis can account for how powerful this could be and a as a determinant in the quality of someone's life

point: True education is about drawing out and unlocking the inherent potential within an individual.
quote: in fact the the exact meaning of the word educate comes from the root word educe it means to bring forth what is within

point: The only genuine disability is a broken spirit that has lost hope, imagination, and curiosity.
quote: i think that the only true disability is a crushed spirit a spirit that's been crushed doesn't have hope
